sentences.text: This medium-sized euornithopod reached a length of six meters and a mass of two tonnes.
Its rear middle back vertebrae feature a depression that is 2.6 times higher than the length of its base.
A skeleton was found in 2013 by researchers from UNED and the Universidad Autónoma de Madrid at the Mas de la Parreta quarry near Morella.
The species Morelladon beltrani was formally named and described in 2015 by José Miguel Gasulla, Fernando Escaso, Iván Narváez, Francisco Ortega, and José Luis Sanz.
The genus name combines the location Morella with the Greek word for tooth.
The species name beltrani honors Victor Beltrán, the quarry owner who cooperated with the scientific research.
Morelladon belongs to the unranked family Iguanodontia.
Morelladon lived in Spain during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 130 million years ago.
The time range for this animal is the Barremian, from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
